items.question: How often must the fire protection test (TEST FIRE 1/2 sw) be performed, per Sect. 4.4.1.1?
options: At least once a day
Before every single flight
Once a week
Only after maintenance actions
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.1 notes the fire protection test must be performed at least once a day, testing both engine fire systems (TEST FIRE 1 sw and TEST FIRE 2 sw) in sequence.

items.question: When must the rotor brake indication check be performed, per Sect. 4.4.1.1?
options: Before flight, after more than 7 days without starting the engines
Before every single flight regardless of elapsed time
Only after maintenance on the rotor brake system
Once per month regardless of flight activity
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.1 states the rotor brake indication check is to be performed before flight after more than 7 days without starting the engines, requiring one person to turn the rotor by hand while a second checks the ROTOR BRAKE indication in the cockpit.

items.question: If T1 (engine temperature) differs by more than a certain amount between the two engines before starting, what should the pilot do, per Sect. 4.4.1.2?
options: If the T1 difference is greater than 20°C, start the engine with the highest T1 first
Always start engine 1 first regardless of T1
Wait until both T1 readings are identical before starting either engine
T1 has no bearing on start sequence
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 notes that if the T1 difference between engines is greater than 20°C, the engine with the highest T1 should be started first.

items.question: How long must the fuel prime pumps be ON before starting the engines, per Sect. 4.4.1.2?
options: At least 10 seconds, to ensure sufficient fuel supply
At least 60 seconds
At least 2 minutes
No minimum time is specified
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 notes that to ensure the engines are supplied sufficiently with fuel, the prime pumps must be on for at least 10 seconds before starting engines.

items.question: During engine start, what minimum TOT increase should be checked/monitored, per Sect. 4.4.1.2?
options: TOT should increase and be checked against a minimum of approximately 720°C
TOT should remain below 400°C throughout the start
TOT is not monitored during the start sequence
TOT should decrease steadily during start
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 requires the pilot to monitor TOT during engine start and check that it increases to at least approximately 720°C, as part of verifying a normal start sequence.

items.question: During the hydraulic check (TEST HYD sw — SYS 1), what caution applies regarding when this check must NOT be performed?
options: The TEST HYD switch must not be operated during flight
The check may only be performed with the rotor stopped
The check must not be performed during cold weather operations
There is no restriction on when the test may be performed
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 CAUTION states the TEST HYD sw must not be operated during flight, and mast moment limits must be observed during the hydraulic check, which must be performed at least once before the first flight of the day.

items.question: What are the two conditions during engine start that trigger an automatic restart attempt (before FADEC upgrade TU149/TU153/TU172), per Sect. 4.4.1.2?
options: If ignition does not take place upon reaching N1 = 18%, the start is interrupted and automatically restarted when N1 decreases to ≤9%
If ignition does not take place upon reaching N1 = 50%, the start is interrupted and restarted at N1 = 20%
There is no automatic restart function; all restarts must be manually initiated
The engine automatically restarts every time N1 exceeds 10%
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 states that (before the FADEC upgrade) if ignition does not take place upon reaching N1 = 18%, the engine automatically interrupts the starting process and performs a restart when N1 has decreased to ≤9%; only one automatic restart will be performed.

items.question: What TOT value, rising abnormally rapidly and approaching 910°C, requires the start to be immediately aborted, per the Abort Start Procedure (Sect. 4.4.1.2)?
options: Above 819°C
Above 700°C
Above 900°C only
Above 600°C
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 CAUTION lists, among the abort-start triggers, TOT rising abnormally rapidly above 819°C and quickly approaching 910°C.

items.question: If the start sequence is interrupted with no automatic restart or shutdown occurring, how long must the pilot wait after the last starter engagement before this is considered an abort condition, per Sect. 4.4.1.2?
options: 15 seconds
5 seconds
60 seconds
2 minutes
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 CAUTION states that if the start sequence is interrupted and an automatic restart or automatic shutdown does not take place at the latest 15 seconds after the last starter engagement, the start must be immediately aborted.

items.question: During starting of the second engine, at what N2 IDLE speed (within what time) should START-UP TST OK appear, per Sect. 4.4.1.2?
options: N2 ≥76%, within approximately 45 seconds
N2 ≥50%, within approximately 10 seconds
N2 ≥100%, within approximately 60 seconds
N2 ≥90%, within approximately 30 seconds
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.2 states that when starting the second engine, upon reaching IDLE speed of N2 ≥76% (within approximately 45 seconds), the FND ML should show START-UP TST OK.

items.question: What ambient temperature condition requires maximum ventilation to be set, per Sect. 4.4.1.3?
options: OAT ≥+30°C
OAT ≥+20°C
OAT ≥+40°C
Maximum ventilation is only needed below 0°C
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.3 System Checks notes that maximum ventilation is required if OAT ≥+30°C.

items.question: Before takeoff, why should the heater be operated in defogging mode until no moisture indications remain on the windows, per the WARNING in Sect. 4.4.1.3?
options: Moisture accumulated in the heater ducting can cause the windshields to fog upon initial heater activation
It is required only for regulatory compliance, with no operational safety reason
It prevents excessive fuel consumption during climb
It is only relevant for night flights
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.3 WARNING states that moisture which may have accumulated in the heater system ducting can cause the windshields to fog upon initial activation of the heater; before takeoff this moisture must be eliminated by operating the heater in defogging mode.

items.question: How must the collective lever be unlatched before performing the AFCS/Avionics Pre-flight Test, per Sect. 4.4.1.3?
options: Unlatch to full down, without physically pushing down on the collective lever to unlatch it
Physically push down on the collective lever to release the latch
The collective must remain latched throughout the test
The collective should be raised to maximum before the test
items.explanation: Sect. 4.4.1.3 instructs: Collective lever — Unlatch, full down, with a NOTE specifically warning not to unlatch the collective lever by physically pushing down on it.

items.question: According to Sect. 4.2.3, what is prohibited regarding mission databases (HTAWS, DMAP, SVS)?
options: Loading or swapping the mission database in flight, since this could lead to loss of the SVS image
Using more than one database type simultaneously
Checking database expiry before flight
There is no restriction on database loading
items.explanation: Sect. 4.2.3 CAUTION states that loading or swapping the mission database in flight could lead to loss of the SVS image, and the database must never be loaded or swapped in flight.

items.question: What items must be checked before dispatching a flight, marked with an asterisk versus not, per Sect. 4.3.1?
options: Asterisked items must be checked before every flight; non-asterisked items only need checking before the first flight of the day (or within a 24-hour cycle for alert/on-call aircraft)
Asterisked items are only checked annually
There is no distinction; all items are checked before every flight
Non-asterisked items are optional and may be skipped entirely
items.explanation: Sect. 4.3.1 states the preflight check shall be completed before each flight, but items not marked with an asterisk need only be checked before the first flight of the day, or within a 24-hour cycle for aircraft on alert/on-call status.

items.question: During the exterior check, what precaution is noted about ground operations and the helicopter battery, per Sect. 4.3.2?
options: To avoid excessive drain on the battery, particularly in cold weather, ground operations should be conducted using an external power unit (EPU), and battery must be connected before EPU connection
The battery should always be disconnected during ground operations
Ground operations have no bearing on battery condition
The EPU should never be used during ground operations
items.explanation: Sect. 4.3.2 notes that to avoid excessive drain on the helicopter battery, particularly during cold weather, all ground operations should be conducted using an external power unit (EPU), and prior to EPU connection the battery must be connected.
